questions.stem: A sum of money at \(10\%\) per annum simple interest amounts to Rs. \(2200\) in \(4\) years. The same sum at \(12\%\) per annum simple interest will amount to how much in \(3\) years?
questions.keySolution:
Let principal = P
Amount after 4 years at 10% = P + (P × 10 × 4)/100 = P + 0.4P = 1.4P = 2200
Therefore, P = 2200/1.4 = Rs. 1571.43
Amount after 3 years at 12% = P + (P × 12 × 3)/100 = P + 0.36P = 1.36P
= 1.36 × 1571.43 = Rs. 2160

questions.stem: The difference between simple interests on a sum of Rs. \(8000\) for \(3\) years at \(8\%\) and \(6\%\) per annum is:
A principal of Rs. \(5000\) gives a simple interest of Rs. \(1000\) in \(4\) years. What will be the simple interest on the same principal in \(6\) years at the same rate?
The simple interest on Rs. \(6000\) at \(10\%\) per annum for \(2\) years is equal to the simple interest on Rs. \(4000\) at what rate per annum for \(3\) years?
questions.keySolution:
SI on Rs. 6000 at 10% for 2 years = (6000 × 10 × 2)/100 = Rs. 1200
Let required rate = R%
SI on Rs. 4000 at R% for 3 years = (4000 × R × 3)/100 = 120R
120R = 1200
R = 10%

questions.stem: If the difference between simple interests on a certain sum at \(12\%\) and \(10\%\) per annum for \(2\) years is Rs. \(80\), find the sum.
questions.keySolution:
Let principal = P
SI at 12% for 2 years = (P × 12 × 2)/100 = 0.24P
SI at 10% for 2 years = (P × 10 × 2)/100 = 0.20P
Difference = 0.24P - 0.20P = 0.04P = 80
P = 80/0.04 = Rs. 2000

questions.stem: A sum invested at \(8\%\) simple interest per annum grows to Rs. \(9200\) in \(3\) years. The same sum at \(10\%\) simple interest per annum will grow to what amount in \(4\) years?
The simple interest on a sum for \(5\) years at \(6\%\) per annum is Rs. \(600\). What will be the simple interest on the same sum for \(8\) years at \(9\%\) per annum?
Two equal sums are lent at \(8\%\) and \(10\%\) simple interest respectively. After \(4\) years, the difference in interests is Rs. \(240\). Find each sum.
questions.keySolution:
Let each sum = P
SI at 10% for 4 years = (P × 10 × 4)/100 = 0.40P
SI at 8% for 4 years = (P × 8 × 4)/100 = 0.32P
Difference = 0.40P - 0.32P = 0.08P = 240
P = 240/0.08 = Rs. 3000

questions.stem: The difference between the simple interests received from two different sources on Rs. \(15000\) for \(3\) years is Rs. \(675\). The difference between their rates is:
questions.keySolution:
Let the rates be R₁% and R₂%
SI difference = P × (R₁ - R₂) × T / 100
675 = 15000 × (R₁ - R₂) × 3 / 100
675 = 450 × (R₁ - R₂)
R₁ - R₂ = 675/450 = 1.5%

questions.stem: The simple interest on a sum at \(7\%\) per annum for \(3\) years is Rs. \(1680\). What will be the simple interest on the same sum at \(9\%\) per annum for \(2\) years?
A sum of money doubles itself in \(10\) years at simple interest. In how many years will it become triple of itself at the same rate?
questions.keySolution:
If sum doubles in 10 years, SI = P and Time = 10 years
Rate = (SI × 100)/(P × T) = (P × 100)/(P × 10) = 10%
For sum to become triple: Amount = 3P, so SI = 2P
Time = (SI × 100)/(P × R) = (2P × 100)/(P × 10) = 20 years

questions.stem: The difference between simple interests on Rs. \(2500\) at \(6\%\) and \(4\%\) per annum for the same period is Rs. \(150\). Find the time period.

A sum of Rs. \(4000\) is lent out in two parts, one at \(8\%\) and the other at \(10\%\) simple interest per annum. If the annual interest is Rs. \(350\), find the sum lent at \(8\%\).
The simple interest on Rs. \(5000\) for \(2\) years at \(6\%\) per annum is equal to simple interest on Rs. \(4000\) at \(10\%\) per annum for how many years?
If the simple interest on Rs. \(1200\) at a certain rate for \(3\) years is Rs. \(432\), what will be the simple interest on Rs. \(1800\) at the same rate for \(2\) years?
A principal becomes Rs. \(1440\) after \(2\) years and Rs. \(1680\) after \(4\) years at simple interest. Find the principal.
questions.keySolution:
In 2 years (from 2nd to 4th year), increase = 1680 - 1440 = Rs. 240
So, SI for 2 years = Rs. 240
SI for 1 year = Rs. 120
SI for 2 years from start = Rs. 240
Principal = Amount after 2 years - SI for 2 years = 1440 - 240 = Rs. 1200

questions.stem: At simple interest, a sum becomes \(6/5\) of itself in \(2\) years. In how many years will it become \(4/3\) of itself?
questions.keySolution:
If sum becomes 6/5 of itself in 2 years:
Amount = (6/5)P, so SI = (6/5)P - P = (1/5)P
Rate = (SI × 100)/(P × T) = [(1/5)P × 100]/(P × 2) = 10%
For sum to become 4/3 of itself: SI = (4/3)P - P = (1/3)P
Time = (SI × 100)/(P × R) = [(1/3)P × 100]/(P × 10) = 10/3 ≈ 3.33 years
Closest answer is 4 years

questions.stem: The simple interest on a certain sum for \(2\) years at \(8\%\) per annum is Rs. \(160\) less than the simple interest on the same sum for \(3\) years at \(12\%\) per annum. Find the sum.
questions.keySolution:
Let the sum = P
SI at 8% for 2 years = (P × 8 × 2)/100 = 0.16P
SI at 12% for 3 years = (P × 12 × 3)/100 = 0.36P
According to question: 0.36P - 0.16P = 160
0.20P = 160
P = Rs. 800
